thread:
leo: catching up from RFC: we need a pragmatic decision for RBAC enforcement on the console query path. core tradeoff: keep auth inline to preserve same-process batching vs move to a uniform sidecar for auditability and KMS integration.

anya: inline adaptor keeps p99 tight and lets us reuse per-process KV caches. downside: auth logic duplicated across runtimes unless we standardize a shared lib.

jamie: sidecar gives single place for audit logs and attestation; easier for Dedicated customers. but extra hop breaks our batching assumption and increases tail.

raj: compliance note: sidecar simplifies HSM attestation and centralized export of signed audit records. adaptor model can still satisfy compliance but requires careful orchestration and log aggregation.

anya: perf numbers from bench: adaptor +0.18ms median, +0.6ms p99. sidecar +0.9ms median, +3.2ms p99. for small dashboard requests that p99 delta matters.

leo: proposal: hybrid approach. 1) implement a pluggable adaptor interface and ship adaptors for latency-sensitive services behind a feature flag. 2) build a lightweight local auth-worker (unix socket) that adaptors call; can run inproc or as a true sidecar. 3) maintain sidecar helm chart for Dedicated. 4) add SLI checks and a canary playbook.

jamie: checklist looks good. add a fallback policy: local cache + deny-by-default when auth backend unreachable.

ci-bot: created issue PLAT-9922 and draft PR #5012 for adaptor+auth-worker (wip) - https://git.internal/repo/pulls/5012 :white_check_mark:

leo: thanks. we'll finalize RFC follow-up doc with migration steps and perf targets tomorrow. raise objections here if any.
